main_body: Thatched hut: a large stepped thatch roof (rows 0-36) over a plank front wall with a door and a window (rows 37-63)
top_band: Light-to-mid straw-yellow thatch roof slope, rows 0-34, in stacked foreshortened courses; the brighter eave band at rows 34-36 forms its front edge
evidence: Reading down the centre column: the thatch roof slope is a large lighter surface seen from above, in many rows of scalloped courses. It ends in a bright eave lip at rows 34-36. Directly below, rows 37-39 are a dark shadow band under the overhang. Then the vertical wall face starts, with a plank door set in a dark frame and a window with a dark inner frame and sill. This matches the reference house roofs, where the sloped roof reads as the top surface above the wall. There is no receding side face. The roof is the dominant top surface, not a thin rim.

style.evidence: The thatch carries about 5 straw tones, from pale highlight through gold and mid to dark brown. Each course has strand and clump texture, which plays the same role as the per-tile scallops on the reference tile roofs. The walls have plank grain in several browns, and the door has dark iron straps, a handle highlight, and a recessed window. Outlines are dark brown and olive, tinted to the adjacent wood and straw rather than neutral black. There are no large flat fills; the grey step at the bottom is small. Density per tile looks comparable to the references. The piece is a little simpler than them but would sit acceptably beside them.
